clusters.name: Your move to the conservatory, 1991–1994
clusters.reason: Around your start at Wexley Conservatory in September 1991, within three years: your wrist injury that stopped your playing and left you lost and low with your grandfather's death and your mother's remarriage all in the months after, a blow-up with your roommate Rafe, your absorption in fixing radios and later your drift at community college with late nights and days asleep, alongside shifts in your relationship toward your father and your anxiety around his notice. By early 1994, when you went to Portugal and found your drive again, the tightness had lifted.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within two and a half years: your own running out of steam for performing and disastrous audition, your move away from Thornbury to Gull Harbour and then to Fenwick with Marisol, your distance from family and friends, your depression once that split apart, your distance from your parents and reliance on friends, and your distance from your grandmother when you visited her sickroom. The period settled as you returned to your therapist and began swimming in early 2004, and then your grandmother died in February.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: your shift to distance from your mother, her pressed visits and your conflict with her when she came to Alder Creek, and your cutoff from her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in August. Though losses of your grandparents sit in these months, the period is your own trouble: your distance, conflict and cutoff from your mother as you left for school.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017, within three years: your shift away from your mother as Wren came along, your cousin Alice's diagnosis with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your aunt Imogen's worsening memory loss and conflicts with your cousin Hal, alongside your own mounting anxiety that you feel you ought to drive your projects forward and your shift to a sleeping pill in late 2019. In the same months, your partner Wren's swamping with events in October 2019, your overfunctioning to settle her, her fusion with her father and brother, and your own symptom of sleeplessness and distance from her at her family's lake house weekend. The shifts around her are reactions to her distress; the period is held by the pile of your own anxiety, your partner's swamping, and the family illnesses that built through 2017 and 2018.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
